{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013m6rqY4rbsDCfrHW5EVLyf","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Kanrad Technologies Inc — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.kantime.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Kanrad Technologies Inc was founded in 1997 as an IT consulting firm handling large-scale software projects for Fortune 500 companies. Around 2010, the company pivoted to a product-focused model and rebranded its post-acute care software as KanTime. The company is headquartered in the U.S. and led by CEO Sundar Kannan, COO Swami Nathan, and CTO Satheesh Kumar.\n     9→\n    10→KanTime positions itself as \"The #1 Home Health and Hospice Enterprise EMR Solution\" and focuses exclusively on the post-acute care market — specifically home health, hospice, palliative care, pediatric home care, private duty home care, and consumer-directed (self-directed) services. Per their website, the platform serves over 912,000 patients, 210,000 users, has processed $12.9 billion in claims, and handles 70 million annual visits. SelectHub ranks KanTime #4 on its top 10 Home Health Software leaderboard. Competitors include Axxess, WellSky, MatrixCare, Alora Healthcare Systems, and Homecare Homebase. Revenue has been estimated at approximately $6.3 million (Kona Equity), suggesting a mid-size company rather than an enterprise vendor. The company holds HITRUST r2, SOC 2 Type 2, ONC Health IT, Surescripts, ACHC, and CHAP certifications/accreditations.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: KanTime Health\n    13→\n    14→CHPL IDs: 11219\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→KanTime Health is a cloud-based (web-based) enterprise EMR and agency management platform purpose-built for post-acute care organizations. It is a single integrated platform covering clinical, operational, financial, and HR functions — not a modular product where components are sold separately. The ONC-certified product covers the full KanTime platform; the certified criteria span clinical documentation (a)(1)-(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14)-(a)(15), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3), patient access (e)(1), (e)(3), clinical quality measures (c)(1)-(c)(3), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10), indicating broad clinical EHR functionality.\n    19→\n    20→The SED intended user description lists \"Clinicians, Physicians, Nurses, Nurse Practitioners and Registered Nurses, Physician Assistants, Medical Assistants and Clinical Backoffice staff\" — consistent with a comprehensive clinical and back-office platform.\n    21→\n    22→### Users & Market\n    23→\n    24→KanTime serves post-acute care agencies of varying sizes, from small home health agencies to large multi-location enterprises. The platform covers six distinct care types from a single system:\n    25→\n    26→- **Home Health** — Medicare/Medicaid certified skilled home health agencies (launched 2012)\n    27→- **Hospice & Palliative Care** — end-of-life and comfort care providers (launched 2016)\n    28→- **Private Duty Home Care** — non-medical personal care services (launched 2010, the original product)\n    29→- **Pediatric Home Care** — specialized pediatric nursing and therapy services\n    30→- **Consumer-Directed / Self-Directed Care** — FMSA, F/EA, Agencies with Choice, FIs, FSEs, and Intermediary Service Organizations (launched 2018)\n    31→\n    32→Their first client was Anova Home Health & Hospice (2012). Day-to-day users include field clinicians (nurses, therapists, aides) using mobile/tablet point-of-care documentation, office staff managing intake/referrals/scheduling, billing and coding staff, QA reviewers, HR/payroll administrators, and agency management using business intelligence dashboards.\n    33→\n    34→The platform operates across virtually all U.S. states and Washington D.C., with EVV integrations covering state Medicaid aggregators nationwide.\n    35→\n    36→### Modules & Functionality\n    37→\n    38→Based on vendor website, product pages, partner listings, and third-party reviews, KanTime Health includes the following major modules and capabilities:\n    39→\n    40→**Intake & Referral Management**\n    41→- Lead generation tracking through assessment, verification, and scheduling of first visit\n    42→- Referral tracking dashboard with partner integrations (CarePort, Cipher Health, Acclivity Health Solutions)\n    43→- Eligibility verification and prior authorization management\n    44→- Interactive dashboard with authorization alerts and deadline tracking\n    45→\n    46→**Scheduling & Staffing**\n    47→- Advanced scheduling engine with drag-and-drop interface\n    48→- Clinician Search Wizard matching caregivers by qualifications, geography, certifications (e.g., Wound Vac, IV training), availability\n    49→- Split shift management offline/online capability\n    58→- Auto-generated 485 plans of care from SOC (Start of Care) assessments\n    59→- OASIS assessment integration with automated documentation linking to OASIS manual\n capability\n    64→- Real-time audit tracking of documentation status\n    65→\n    66→**E-Prescribing (KRx Module)**\n    67→- DEA-certified EPCS (Electronic Prescribing for Controlled Substances)\n signs\n   144→- Treatment plans\n   145→- Medication lists and prescribing history (via Surescripts integration, up to 1 year)\n   146→- Prescription records (including controlled substances via Benchmarking data\n   178→- Multi-location aggregated reporting\n   179→\n   180→**Notable observations:**\n   181→- KanTime is a comprehensive all-in-one platform — billing, HR/payroll, scheduling, This means the EHI export should theoretically cover all of these data domains.\n   182→- The Surescripts integration for medication history and e-prescribing means prescription and medication data flows through the system.\n   183→- The vendor website does not prominently mention lab ordering/results, diagnostic imaging, or patient portal messaging as features — these are less typical for home health/hospice settings but the (e)(1) certification for patient access/VDT suggests some patient-facing data access exists.\n   184→- The (a)(14) certification criterion (implantable device list) is notable for a home health/hospice product and suggests the system tracks implantable device information.\n   185→- The (a)(12) certification (family health history) is also somewhat unusual for post-acute care and indicates this data type is supported.\n   186→\n   187→---\n   188→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. Around 2010, the company pivoted to a product-focused model and rebranded its post-acute care software as KanTime. The company is headquartered in the U.S. and led by CEO Sundar Kannan, COO Swami Nathan, and CTO Satheesh Kumar.\n\nKanTime positions itself as \"The #1 Home Health and Hospice Enterprise EMR Solution\" and focuses exclusively on the post-acute care market — specifically home health, hospice, palliative care, pediatric home care, private duty home care, and consumer-directed (self-directed) services. Per their website, the platform serves over 912,000 patients, 210,000 users, has processed $12.9 billion in claims, and handles 70 million annual visits. SelectHub ranks KanTime #4 on its top 10 Home Health Software leaderboard. Competitors include Axxess, WellSky, MatrixCare, Alora Healthcare Systems, and Homecare Homebase. Revenue has been estimated at approximately $6.3 million (Kona Equity), suggesting a mid-size company rather than an enterprise vendor. The company holds HITRUST r2, SOC 2 Type 2, ONC Health IT, Surescripts, ACHC, and CHAP certifications/accreditations.\n\n## Product: KanTime Health\n\nCHPL IDs: 11219\n\n### What It Is\n\nKanTime Health is a cloud-based (web-based) enterprise EMR and agency management platform purpose-built for post-acute care organizations. It is a single integrated platform covering clinical, operational, financial, and HR functions — not a modular product where components are sold separately. The ONC-certified product covers the full KanTime platform; the certified criteria span clinical documentation (a)(1)-(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14)-(a)(15), transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3), patient access (e)(1), (e)(3), clinical quality measures (c)(1)-(c)(3), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)-(g)(10), indicating broad clinical EHR functionality.\n\nThe SED intended user description lists \"Clinicians, Physicians, Nurses, Nurse Practitioners and Registered Nurses, Physician Assistants, Medical Assistants and Clinical Backoffice staff\" — consistent with a comprehensive clinical and back-office platform.\n\n### Users & Market\n\nKanTime serves post-acute care agencies of varying sizes, from small home health agencies to large multi-location enterprises. The platform covers six distinct care types from a single system:\n\n- **Home Health** — Medicare/Medicaid certified skilled home health agencies (launched 2012)\n- **Hospice & Palliative Care** — end-of-life and comfort care providers (launched 2016)\n- **Private Duty Home Care** — non-medical personal care services (launched 2010, the original product)\n- **Pediatric Home Care** — specialized pediatric nursing and therapy services\n- **Consumer-Directed / Self-Directed Care** — FMSA, F/EA, Agencies with Choice, FIs, FSEs, and Intermediary Service Organizations (launched 2018)\n\nTheir first client was Anova Home Health & Hospice (2012). Day-to-day users include field clinicians (nurses, therapists, aides) using mobile/tablet point-of-care documentation, office staff managing intake/referrals/scheduling, billing and coding staff, QA reviewers, HR/payroll administrators, and agency management using business intelligence dashboards.\n\nThe platform operates across virtually all U.S. states and Washington D.C., with EVV integrations covering state Medicaid aggregators nationwide.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website, product pages, partner listings, and third-party reviews, KanTime Health includes the following major modules and capabilities:\n\n**Intake & Referral Management**\n- Lead generation tracking through assessment, verification, and scheduling of first visit\n- Referral tracking dashboard with partner integrations (CarePort, Cipher Health, Acclivity Health Solutions)\n- Eligibility verification and prior authorization management\n- Interactive dashboard with authorization alerts and deadline tracking\n\n**Scheduling & Staffing**\n- Advanced scheduling engine with drag-and-drop interface\n- Clinician Search Wizard matching caregivers by qualifications, geography, certifications (e.g., Wound Vac, IV training), availability\n- Split shift management across multiple payers/services\n- Real-time patient and clinician calendar views\n- Multi-discipline client calendars\n- Ad hoc visit tracking (clock in/out for unscheduled visits)\n- Late clock-in alerts\n- Need-to-hire indicators\n\n**Clinical Point-of-Care Documentation**\n- Mobile/tablet documentation (Android and iOS) with offline/online capability\n- Auto-generated 485 plans of care from SOC (Start of Care) assessments\n- OASIS assessment integration with automated documentation linking to OASIS manual\n- Hard stops and mandatory fields for compliance\n- Vital signs, assessments, visit notes, treatment plans capture\n- Autofill for repeated data\n- Electronic signature capability\n- Real-time audit tracking of documentation status\n\n**E-Prescribing (KRx Module)**\n- DEA-certified EPCS (Electronic Prescribing for Controlled Substances)\n- Integration with Surescripts pharmacy network (nationwide)\n- On-demand medication history retrieval (up to 1 year via Surescripts)\n- Drug-to-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking via FirstDataBank\n- 24/7 mobile prescription capability\n- HIPAA compliant\n\n**Order Tracking**\n- Missing documentation tracking\n- Physician order compliance monitoring\n- Electronic physician order faxing with auto-mapping\n\n**Quality Assurance**\n- Active audit capabilities for real-time documentation tracking\n- Compliance monitoring for state and federal regulations\n- Standardized documentation enforcement\n\n**IDT (Interdisciplinary Team) Management**\n- Secure collaboration across all care roles\n- Shared access to care plans and notes\n- Streamlined IDT meeting workflow (particularly for hospice)\n- HIPAA-compliant messaging for staff communication\n\n**Hospice-Specific Features**\n- Bereavement management with customized follow-up alerts\n- Volunteer management tracking (5% volunteer service requirement)\n- Hospice benefit period management\n- HIS (Hospice Item Set) data collection\n- Non-billable service tracking\n\n**Billing & Revenue Cycle Management**\n- Full billing lifecycle: charge entry, claim submission, remittance, accounts receivable\n- Automated 837 batch claim generation\n- Payer-specific billing rules to reduce errors\n- Secondary payer processing\n- Denial management and timely filing tracking\n- Direct clearinghouse interfaces (Waystar, Ability)\n- Advanced financial reporting across branches and service lines\n- Integration with multiple billing/payment partners (Availity, Change Healthcare, Claim MD, HHAeXchange, Sandata)\n\n**HR & Payroll**\n- Payroll as a Service (PaaS) integrated with scheduling\n- Timesheet management with clinician lock pay period\n- Pay rate dispute resolution workflow\n- Payment preview system\n- Employee credential/license expiration alerts\n- Benefits tracking\n- Integration with external payroll providers (ADP, Accufund, Americas Back Office, Apex, Asure, BambooHR, BBSI, Ceridian)\n\n**Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)**\n- GPS and telephony-based visit verification\n- Cures Act compliant\n- Integrated with state aggregators across all 50 states + D.C.\n- Proprietary EVV plus integrations with CellTrak, CareBridge\n\n**Business Intelligence (KanTime+)**\n- Clinical, financial, and operational KPI dashboards\n- Drill-down analytics for management\n- Multi-branch/multi-location reporting\n- Benchmarking integration (Activated Insights partner)\n\n**Additional Integrations**\n- Pharmacy: AvantumRx, BetterRx (particularly for hospice)\n- Medical supplies/DME: Cardinal Health, Capstone HME\n- Telehealth capabilities (referenced in partner categories)\n- CRM and referral management partners\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the modules and features described above, KanTime Health stores and manages the following categories of data:\n\n**Patient/Clinical Data:**\n- Patient demographics and contact information\n- Clinical assessments (including OASIS assessments for home health, HIS for hospice)\n- Plans of care (auto-generated 485s)\n- Visit notes and point-of-care documentation\n- Vital signs\n- Treatment plans\n- Medication lists and prescribing history (via Surescripts integration, up to 1 year)\n- Prescription records (including controlled substances via EPCS)\n- Drug interaction and allergy data (via FirstDataBank)\n- Physician orders\n- Care coordination notes and IDT meeting documentation\n- Bereavement records (hospice)\n\n**Administrative/Operational Data:**\n- Referral and intake records\n- Scheduling data (visits, shifts, caregiver assignments)\n- Authorization and eligibility records\n- Electronic visit verification data (GPS coordinates, timestamps, telephony records)\n- QA audit trails\n- HIPAA-compliant staff messaging\n\n**Financial Data:**\n- Billing claims (837 format)\n- Remittance and payment records\n- Accounts receivable\n- Denial tracking\n- Payer information and billing rules\n- Financial reports across branches/service lines\n\n**HR/Workforce Data:**\n- Employee/caregiver records\n- Credentials and license expiration tracking\n- Timesheets and payroll data\n- Benefits information\n- Pay rate records\n\n**Analytics/Reporting Data:**\n- Clinical, financial, and operational KPIs\n- Benchmarking data\n- Multi-location aggregated reporting\n\n**Notable observations:**\n- KanTime is a comprehensive all-in-one platform — billing, HR/payroll, scheduling, clinical documentation, e-prescribing, and EVV are all integrated rather than separate products. This means the EHI export should theoretically cover all of these data domains.\n- The Surescripts integration for medication history and e-prescribing means prescription and medication data flows through the system.\n- The vendor website does not prominently mention lab ordering/results, diagnostic imaging, or patient portal messaging as features — these are less typical for home health/hospice settings but the (e)(1) certification for patient access/VDT suggests some patient-facing data access exists.\n- The (a)(14) certification criterion (implantable device list) is notable for a home health/hospice product and suggests the system tracks implantable device information.\n- The (a)(12) certification (family health history) is also somewhat unusual for post-acute care and indicates this data type is supported.\n\n---\n","numLines":188,"startLine":1,"totalLines":188}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FrC8dXAndDoyJJo16ZwqZo","type":"tool_result","content":"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\nKantime Health supports the export of electronic health information (EHI) based on user roles\nfor both clinical and billing data.\n\nSingle or Multi-Patient EHI Export\nUsers who have access to EHI export authorization will be able to export clinical data using the\nCCDA 2.1 Release 2 standard.\nThe billing user role will facilitate the process for users to extract patient claims and payments in\nCSV format export.\n\nExported File Formats\n●\n●\n\nClinical data is exported as CCDA 2.1 Release 2 USCDI v1.\nBilling data is exported as CSV, XLSX or PDF.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3f685423-11f9-466a-aecf-876d89860915","uuid":"ad406cec-632d-4203-85b7-70338550be7b","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\nKantime Health supports the export of electronic health information (EHI) based on user roles\nfor both clinical and billing data.\n\nSingle or Multi-Patient EHI Export\nUsers who have access to EHI export authorization will be able to export clinical data using the\nCCDA 2.1 Release 2 standard.\nThe billing user role will facilitate the process for users to extract patient claims and payments in\nCSV format export.\n\nExported File Formats\n●\n●\n\nClinical data is exported as CCDA 2.1 Release 2 USCDI v1.\nBilling data is exported as CSV, XLSX or PDF.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TN6usgrzxigpMxufgDbddt","type":"tool_result","content":" Utah has chosen an interim Open EVV Model without requiring integration with an Aggregator.  Agencies can use Cures Act Compliant EVV Vendors like KanTime and be subject to periodic State Audit of EVV data collection through submission of a formatted export to the State.  KanTime has generated this export within the specified format for Utah and it is in use with KanTime agency customers.  You may continue using KanTime software solutions to manage your agency in Utah. \n South Dakota has chosen the Closed EVV model that forces all agency users to use their selected vendor only.  Agencies providing services that require EVV must use Therap as their EVV vendor.  KanTime&#8217;s Home Healthcare EMR has generated a custom formatted export of schedules data for transmission to Therap which is the sole method that Therap will support.  This export method in use by KanTime agency customers in South Dakota.   You may continue using KanTime software solutions to manage your agency in South Dakota. \nCSV Manual Export as | The #1 Home Health and Hospice Enterprise EMR Solution\",\"url\":\"https://kantime.com/\"}]\n\nBased on the web search results, I found documentation related to KanTime, including KanTime Patient API Documentation that describes how to access patient data using KanTime Patient API, which allows registered users to query the EHR for patient data and returns a JSON object with status and embedded CCDA XML.\n\nHowever, the search results did not return a specific KanTime EHI export documentation data dictionary. The results included EHI export documentation from other health IT vendors (ModMed, Practice Fusion, Oracle/Cerner, CGM APRIMA, and Veradigm), but not KanTime's specific EHI export data dictionary.\n\nThe closest match was KanTime Patient API Documentation (dated March 2024), which is available at kantime.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/KanTime_Patient_API.pdf.\n\nIf you're looking for KanTime's EHI export documentation and data dictionary specifically, you may need to:\n- Contact KanTime directly for their EHI export documentation\n- Check the KanTime website's resources or documentation section\n- Check if it's available through your KanTime account or support portal\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TFHFzDxVt4s7wVF7b84GAo","type":"tool_result","content":"KanTime Patient API Documentation\nVersion 1.0\n\nIntroduction\nThis document describes how to access patient data using KanTime Patient API. Registered users can use this API to\nquery the EHR for patient data. The API returns a JSON object with status and embedded CCDA XML. API examples below\nshow how to access the API using curl.\n\nRequirements\nUser must be an authorized user of the KanTime EHR or user must have access to the patient portal\nAccess to REST client (use curl, or any other programmatic REST client)\nAbility to parse JSON and CCDA\n\nAPI\nFollowing sections describe the available API. Base URL for accessing the API is:\nhttps://staging.kantimehealth.net/phx/api/papi/api\n\nAuthenticate user\nUse credentials which are used for KanTime EHR or Patient Portal to authenticate with this API. API returns a token that\nwill be used for all other API calls.\nUsername and password have to be encoded in Base64 with the call to curl. Use Basic authorization header for curl.\nEndpoint:\nPOST https://staging.kantimehealth.net/phx/api/papi/api/v1/Patient/authenticateuser\nExample:\ncurl --location --request POST\n'https://staging.kantimehealth.net/phx/api/papi/api/v1/Patient/authenticateuser'\n\\\n--header 'Authorization: Basic YWxiZXJ0QGthbnJhZC5jb206RGVtb0AxMjM='\nResponse:\n{\n\"MRN\": null,\n\"PatientID\": null,\n\"Token\":\n\"eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjQ2NzhGOTY3RUQyQTQwOEYwMzUwNUEwM0M5OUFDRTcyMUE2QTQwMTUiLCJ0eXAiO\niJKV1QifQ.eyJzdWIiOiJhbGJlcnRAa2FucmFkLmNvbSIsImF1ZCI6WyJwYXRfYXBpIl0sImZpcnN0bmFtZSI6IkFsYmVydCIsImxhc3\nRuYW1lIjoiRGF2aXMiLCJ1aWQiOiI1MDg2OTAiLCJwaWQiOiIxMDAwNCIsIm5iZiI6MTcxMTAzNDM3OCwiZXhwIjoxNzExMD\nM3OTc4LCJpc3MiOiJodHRwczovL3N0YWdpbmcua2FudGltZWhlYWx0aC5uZXQvaWRlbnRpdHkvdjIifQ.EuslsS7EuxTRigdTvhz\nNY-nAdsTbW2puD01eWL-qzFmXi_eXFxakaF_Oj10qox77bU5zf3xVSAH6-6-Kc9vYO8JLu7A5d_c1gIjuevzUGkZ2z73Kp4IuASiZ\ndtNrzSQLvnO1327AWzaLAE2n6qi4XFPpnYcvRNgsnAgY9lPZxAsOMRSWUY6vO4a6QxWpnzZ2_R21cTyyLN2ZDo2zoz-zBAoYz\n7FwikTdvcJsqFW-A8QXYd4Lm5hhH_eMReDWaK38qnqaH6gZCDXf8LZ2WrVg-n6gTDl4dRYqI_z15ad08IJMs49nJy_GqMEDH\n\n\fULS3HBL8J7vcNU5B8giTjrHrhtPzgsEEsb384z0mQc_f6ou21QoOWIJQ7NucOZNyXKOLPK2_Zfal7wRGpsWOVVo-IU4DxYAICYJ\nhQ0MQk2uyxSaYKEcstgJEiAmYUdLup6KvFagjYAoYkCc0qjjHrKLqG18JICDNg3Jy7ibwSzq9Myv0IqVCZdx1ng3CPWUAfIYQZKg\nq4ljZ82zzZI5JBrIgfLflpE_hW1qwG12FKBUSsEDrn1U-XJ4fzj1VTwvqjw3sfJEDGQ17urOeSgURvGTVhwgL14y3SvopSCMwqG8i\nO98ka9G0TA3Nj8GmQRgiXSv80h6jOC1lzHNDp3h2NZ7OOpAaZTuiDhEfadMZ-QWAjCnolQ\",\n\"StatusCode\": 0,\n\"StatusDescription\": null\n}\nStore the value Token. The command above queries for data between Jan 1 2016\n(2016-01-01) and Jan 1 2018 (2018-01-01)\nResponse will be the same CCDA as above, except all clinical data will be restricted to date of service between Jan 1 2016\nand Jan 1 2018.\n\nError Codes\n●\n\n●\n\nUnauthorized access:\nIf the user credentials are invalid, following error will be generated with code: 401\n{\"message\": \"Unauthorized token request. Invalid Credentials provided\"}\nIf token is invalid/expired, following error will be generated with code: 401\n{Invalid token provided}\nPatient not found:\nIf the patient record does not exist for the patient being requested, following error will be generated\n{\n\"patients\": [],\n\"StatusCode\": 0,\n\"StatusDescription\": \"Patient not found\"\n}\n\n●\n\nUser no rights to access patient:\nIf user has no rights to access patient, following error will be generated\n{\n\"patients\": null,\n\"StatusCode\": -1,\n\"StatusDescription\": \"Invalid input, Patient/representative should have access to search\nhis mapped patient data only.\"\n}\n\n●\n\nMore than one patient found with search criteria and logged in user is patient/patient representative\nIf more than one patient is found when logged in with patient/patient representative credentials, following error\nwill be generated\n{\n\n\"patients\": null,\n\"StatusCode\": -1,\n\"StatusDescription\": \"Invalid input, Patient/representative should have access to search\nhis mapped patient data only.\"\n}\n\n●\n\nCCCDA Section not found:\nIf the user calls service patientData with invalid section name, following error will be generated\n<Message>Invalid section name: careteams</Message>","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3f685423-11f9-466a-aecf-876d89860915","uuid":"37900e87-1188-4c6b-b06a-205981491e37","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"KanTime Patient API Documentation\nVersion 1.0\n\nIntroduction\nThis document describes how to access patient data using KanTime Patient API. Registered users can use this API to\nquery the EHR for patient data. The API returns a JSON object with status and embedded CCDA XML. API examples below\nshow how to access the API using curl.\n\nRequirements\nUser must be an authorized user of the KanTime EHR or user must have access to the patient portal\nAccess to REST client (use curl, or any other programmatic REST client)\nAbility to parse JSON and CCDA\n\nAPI\nFollowing sections describe the available API. Base URL for accessing the API is:\nhttps://staging.kantimehealth.net/phx/api/papi/api\n\nAuthenticate user\nUse credentials which are used for KanTime EHR or Patient Portal to authenticate with this API. API returns a token that\nwill be used for all other API calls.\nUsername and password have to be encoded in Base64 with the call to curl. v1.0\nINTRODUCTION\n\nIn this documentation we will list all the steps required to access protected health information based on the documentation of an open API. The\nAPI makes health information broadly available using FHIR®, a set of clinical interoperability resources under the umbrella of the HL7 standards\norganization. FHIR is based on common web standards can be reached through a RESTful protocol in which each FHIR resource has a known\nURL. This document describes OAuth 2.0 for client applications to authorize, authenticate, and integrate with FHIR-based data systems.\nWe follow Smart-On-FHIR authentication (OAuth2) and authorization. (Ref: https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/STU2/)\n\nFHIR Endpoints\nNote: Production and Test Server endpoints are subject to change.\n\nProduction Endpoint\n•\n\nFHIR : https://qafhir.kantimehealth.net:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\n\n•\n\nAuthentication Server: https://qaoauth.kantimehealth.net/\n\nTest Server Endpoint\n•\n•\n\nFHIR : https://qafhir.kantimehealth.net:9443/fhirserver/fhir/\nAuthentication Server: https://qaoauth.kantimehealth.net/\n\nTypes of Smart-On-FHIR applications\n•\n\nStandalone App : SMART on FHIR confidential client with a patient context, refresh token, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity\ntoken.\n\n•\n\nEHR Embedded app: Demonstrate the ability to perform an EHR launch to a SMART on FHIR\n\n•\n\nSmart Backend Services App (Multi-patient authorization and API) : These are server-to-server backend applications e.g. Export\nclinical data for multiple patients in a group. This app is system level app without any UI.\n\nTypes of Authentications supported\n•\n\nSymmetric (“client secret”) authentication\n\n•\n\nAsymmetric (“private key JWT”) authentication\n\n•\n\nPublic {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_0139aFiAdnY54qXXDuAVPJJN","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01SFsxX3t35Mn1Dd81d1AJ4k","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/kanrad-technologies-inc--kantime-health/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Kanrad Technologies Inc — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://kantime.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf\n- CHPL IDs: 11219\n- Product: KanTime Health v1.0\n- Certification date: 2023-01-18\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n### Step 1: Probe the registered URL\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://kantime.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\nResult: HTTP 200, Content-Type: application/pdf, Content-Length: 42570 bytes. Direct PDF download — no redirects.\n\n### Step 2: Download and verify the PDF\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://kantime.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf\nfile downloads/EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf  # PDF document, version 1.4, 1 page(s)\npdfinfo downloads/EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf  # 1 page, 42570 bytes, produced by \"Skia/PDF m121 Google Docs Renderer\"\n```\nConfirmed: valid 1-page PDF titled \"EHI Tool Documentation.\"\n\n### Step 3: Extract and read the PDF text\nThe entire document reads:\n> Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export\n> Kantime Health supports the export of electronic health information (EHI) based on user roles for both clinical and billing data.\n>\n> **Single or Multi-Patient EHI Export**\n> Users who have access to EHI export authorization will be able to export clinical data using the CCDA 2.1 Release 2 standard.\n> The billing user role will facilitate the process for users to extract patient claims and payments in CSV format export.\n>\n> **Exported File Formats**\n> - Clinical data is exported as CCDA 2.1 Release 2 USCDI v1.\n> - Billing data is exported as CSV, XLSX or PDF.\n\nNo URLs, no embedded files, no attachments in the PDF.\n\n### Step 4: Check the ONC Regulatory Compliance page for additional docs\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://kantime.com/care-type/onc-regulatory-compliance/\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o /tmp/kantime-onc.html\n```\nFound an \"EHI Export Documentation\" section that says: \"Documentation on the 170.315 (b)(10) EHI Export output format for each Kanrad Technologies ONC Certified solutions is provided below.\" with a link to the same PDF. The page also links to:\n- `KanTime_Patient_API.pdf` — REST API documentation for accessing patient CCDA data\n- `SmartOnFHIRAPIDoc.pdf` — SMART on FHIR API documentation (66 pages, for (g)(10))\n- `fhir-base-urls-1.json` — FHIR R4 endpoint Bundle\n- `KanTime_Health_Patient_API_TOU.pdf` — Terms of Use (not downloaded, not EHI export content)\n\n### Step 5: Download the Patient API PDF\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://kantime.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/KanTime_Patient_API.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/KanTime_Patient_API.pdf\n```\n14-page PDF (255KB). This describes a REST API for exporting clinical data as CCDA XML — the same mechanism referenced in the EHI export documentation. Endpoints include:\n- `POST .../v1/Patient/authenticateuser` — authenticate with KanTime credentials\n- `POST .../v1/Patient/patientsearch` — search patients by MRN, DOB, name\n- `POST .../v1/Patient/patientccda` — retrieve full CCDA for a patient (with optional date range)\n- `POST .../v1/Patient/patientdata/{sectionname}` — retrieve specific clinical sections\n\nAvailable CCDA sections: demographics, careteam, allergies, assessments, encounters, functionalstatus, goals, healthconcerns, immunizations, medicalequipment, medications, mentalstatus, planoftreatment, problem, procedures, reasonforreferral, results, socialhistory, vitalsigns, consultationnote, progressnote, historyandphysicalnote.\n\n### Step 6: Download FHIR-related files for context\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://kantime.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/SmartOnFHIRAPIDoc.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/SmartOnFHIRAPIDoc.pdf\ncurl -sL \"https://kantime.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/fhir-base-urls-1.json\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/fhir-base-urls-1.json\n```\nThe SMART on FHIR doc (66 pages) covers the (g)(10) FHIR API — standard US Core resources (Patient, AllergyIntolerance, CarePlan, CareTeam, Condition, Device, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Goal, Immunization, Medication, Procedure, Observation, etc.). It does NOT mention (b)(10) or EHI export. The FHIR base URLs JSON is a FHIR Bundle with 2 organization endpoints.\n\n### Step 7: Search for additional documentation\n- Checked `https://kantime.com/certifications-accreditations-and-compliance/` — no additional EHI-specific links beyond what's on the ONC page.\n- Checked sitemap (`sitemap_index.xml`) — no EHI-related pages.\n- `https://kantime.com/interoperability/` and `https://kantime.com/ehi/` — both return 404.\n- Web search for \"kantime.com EHI export documentation data dictionary\" — no additional KanTime EHI docs found.\n- Wayback Machine check — no archived alternative versions.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of:\n\n1. **A 1-page PDF** (`EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf`, 42KB) that describes the export at the highest possible level: clinical data exports as CCDA 2.1 Release 2 (USCDI v1), and billing data exports as CSV, XLSX, or PDF. That is the complete content — no data dictionary, no field definitions, no schema, no examples, no instructions for how to actually perform the export.\n\n2. **A 14-page Patient API PDF** (`KanTime_Patient_API.pdf`, 255KB) that documents a REST API for retrieving clinical data as CCDA XML. This is the technical mechanism for the clinical side of the EHI export. It provides authentication details, search parameters, and sample CCDA output. The API supports retrieving the full CCDA or specific clinical sections, with optional date range filtering. The sample response shows a standard C-CDA \"Summary of Care\" document. This API requires authentication (Basic Auth to get a JWT, then Bearer token for API calls).\n\n3. **A 66-page SMART on FHIR API doc** (`SmartOnFHIRAPIDoc.pdf`, 686KB) and a **FHIR base URLs JSON** (`fhir-base-urls-1.json`, 4KB) — these are (g)(10) FHIR API documentation, NOT (b)(10) EHI export docs. They cover standard US Core FHIR resources and are included for completeness but are a separate certification requirement.\n\n**What is completely absent:**\n- Any documentation of the billing data export (CSV/XLSX/PDF): what fields are included, what the columns mean, what data is covered\n- A data dictionary of any kind — no table definitions, no field descriptions, no schema\n- Any documentation of non-USCDI clinical data: OASIS assessments, HIS data, care plans (485s), visit notes, EVV data, HR/payroll data, intake/referral data\n- Sample export files\n- Instructions for how to perform the export within the KanTime UI\n- Screenshots of the export interface\n- Schema files (XSD, JSON Schema, etc.)\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nKanTime Health is a comprehensive post-acute care platform storing clinical, billing, HR/payroll, scheduling, and operational data. The EHI export documentation reveals a two-track approach:\n\n**Track 1 — Clinical data via CCDA 2.1:** The Patient API documents export of clinical data as C-CDA documents. The available sections map directly to standard USCDI v1 clinical data classes:\n- Demographics, allergies, care team, encounters\n- Problems/conditions, medications, immunizations, procedures\n- Vital signs, lab results, goals, health concerns\n- Social history, functional status, mental status\n- Clinical notes (consultation, progress, H&P)\n- Plan of treatment, medical equipment, assessments\n\nThis covers the standard clinical summary but is **explicitly limited to what C-CDA supports.** It does NOT address specialty-specific data that KanTime stores.\n\n**Track 2 — Billing data via CSV/XLSX/PDF:** The 1-page EHI doc states that billing users can export \"patient claims and payments.\" There is zero documentation of what this export contains — no field definitions, no column descriptions, no sample files.\n\n**Major data domains from the product research that are NOT addressed in the export documentation:**\n\n| Data Domain | Status |\n|-------------|--------|\n| OASIS assessments (home health) | Not mentioned — these are KanTime's core clinical assessment instruments |\n| HIS data (hospice) | Not mentioned |\n| Plans of care / 485s | Not mentioned (plan of treatment in CCDA is generic, not the auto-generated 485) |\n| Visit notes / point-of-care documentation | Partially covered by CCDA clinical notes, but likely incomplete for the full breadth of visit documentation |\n| Scheduling data | Not mentioned |\n| E-prescribing records (KRx module) | Medications in CCDA, but prescribing workflow/history not documented |\n| Authorization / eligibility records | Not mentioned |\n| EVV data (GPS, telephony) | Not mentioned |\n| Intake / referral records | Not mentioned |\n| QA audit data | Not mentioned |\n| HR / payroll / credential data | Not mentioned (and likely not EHI, but credential-linked care data may be) |\n| Bereavement management (hospice) | Not mentioned |\n| IDT meeting documentation | Not mentioned |\n| Order tracking | Not mentioned |\n\nThe export appears to be a **USCDI v1 clinical summary + an undocumented billing export.** This is a significant gap for a (b)(10) certification, which requires export of ALL electronic health information — not just the USCDI clinical subset.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Clinical:** C-CDA 2.1 Release 2, USCDI v1. This is a recognized standard but is inherently limited to what C-CDA can represent. Post-acute care data (OASIS, HIS, EVV, 485 plans, specialized visit notes) does not map cleanly into C-CDA sections.\n- **Billing:** CSV, XLSX, or PDF — format not documented. No schema or field definitions.\n- **No bulk/batch mechanism documented:** The Patient API is a per-patient REST call. There is no documented way to export data for all patients or to perform a bulk export. The EHI PDF mentions \"Single or Multi-Patient EHI Export\" but provides no details on how multi-patient export works.\n\nCould a third party reconstruct a patient record from this export? For the USCDI clinical slice — partially, yes, via the CCDA. For the full patient record as stored in KanTime — no. Billing data format is undocumented. Specialty-specific clinical data (OASIS, HIS, care plans) is not addressed at all.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThis is among the most minimal EHI export documentation one could produce:\n\n- **The core EHI document is 1 page with 5 sentences.** It describes what formats are used but nothing about what data is included, how to access the export, or what the exported files look like.\n- **No data dictionary exists** — neither for the CCDA sections nor for the billing CSV export.\n- **No sample files** are provided.\n- **No user instructions** for how to perform the export within the KanTime application.\n- **No screenshots** of the export interface.\n- The Patient API PDF is more substantive (14 pages with curl examples and sample CCDA output) but it documents the API mechanism, not the data content. It tells you how to call the API, not what clinical data you'll get back beyond section names.\n- The documentation appears to be a compliance checkbox rather than a genuine effort to enable data portability.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Field-level documentation:** None. Not even table/entity names for the billing export.\n- **Value sets:** Not documented. The CCDA will use standard C-CDA value sets, but any KanTime-specific coded fields are undocumented.\n- **Relationships between entities:** Not documented.\n- **Versioning:** The EHI PDF appears unchanged since its upload date (November 2023, modified December 2023). The Patient API PDF was uploaded March 2024.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://kantime.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- `https://kantime.com/interoperability/` — 404\n- `https://kantime.com/ehi/` — 404\n- WordPress uploads directory listing blocked (403)\n- Sitemap mostly empty, no EHI-related page URLs found\n- No additional EHI documentation found via web search\n- The SmartOnFHIR API doc and FHIR base URLs are (g)(10) artifacts, not (b)(10) EHI export documentation. Downloaded for completeness but they don't document the EHI export.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1913,"cache_read_input_tokens":67656,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1913},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3f685423-11f9-466a-aecf-876d89860915","uuid":"a9480a51-978a-4de6-aedd-3777b15e82f9"}

Here's a summary:\n\n**KanTime Health EHI Export Documentation — Collection Summary**\n\n**What was found:** Extremely minimal documentation.\n\n1. **EHI_Tool_Documentation.pdf** (1 page, 42KB) — The registered (b)(10) doc. Five sentences stating clinical data exports as CCDA 2.1 and billing data as CSV/XLSX/PDF. No data dictionary, no field definitions, no instructions.\n\n2. **KanTime_Patient_API.pdf** (14 pages, 255KB) — REST API docs for retrieving patient clinical data as CCDA XML. This is the technical mechanism for the clinical export, with curl examples and sample CCDA output covering ~22 clinical sections (allergies, meds, vitals, problems, encounters, etc.).\n\n3. **SmartOnFHIRAPIDoc.pdf** + **fhir-base-urls-1.json** — (g)(10) FHIR API docs, not the (b)(10) export.
